title: Society Wives — Character Attraction & Relationship Audit
scope: Reusable for all five women's office, society, family, friends' husbands and short-term attraction routes. Start with Ankita.

questions.question: Is she the only woman in her team, or who are the other female colleagues?
What is her exact job title, reporting line and daily team structure?
Who reports to her and who has authority over her?
Which colleagues are teammates, mentors, rivals or friends?
Which characters genuinely need a work reason to interact with her?
Is she considered beautiful or striking in this fictional world, and by whom?
What visible features stand out: face, hair, figure, bust, waist, hips, posture or saree styling?
What office outfits and personal style choices fit her profession?
Which qualities beyond looks make her attractive: confidence, humour, kindness or skill?
Do different characters notice different aspects of her appearance and presence?
Which adult men are physically attracted to her, and how strong is it?
Which men have genuine romantic feelings rather than only an occasional attraction?
Which men experience only a brief, one-time impression?
Which men admire her professionally without romantic or sexual interest?
What is each man's personal reason for being attracted to her?
Is any attraction one-sided, secret, mistaken or mutually acknowledged?
Does an attraction originate from office contact, society contact or a cross-house introduction?
Has anyone acted on his feelings, or is everything still latent?
Whom does she find physically attractive, and why?
Whose personality or intellect might intrigue her romantically?
Who is important to her but does not attract her?
Can her interest change independently from a man's feelings?
What would make her notice or reconsider a person without crossing boundaries?
What is the first believable interaction for every pair?
What is the first small crack: a compliment, private joke, gratitude or accidental misunderstanding?
How many ordinary encounters are needed before a potential romance feels earned?
What distinct mini-arc title and episode titles belong to each character pair?
What event could move a one-time impression into repeated curiosity?
What happens if the interest stays unrequited or fades?
How will other coworkers notice changes and what realistic workplace consequences might follow?
How do work seniority, supervision and power differences constrain every romance?
Is any contact unwanted, and how does she set or enforce a boundary?
Where are the characters at the same time on the shared story calendar?
Does a character's appearance in this episode match their approved prior timeline?
What information is canon, user-approved draft, or an unapproved suggestion?
Which relationships and scenes should remain purely professional?
Does this man want a one-time encounter, a brief casual relationship, or only have a fleeting attraction?
Does the woman independently want any short-term intimacy, or is the desire entirely one-sided?
Is the one-night interest a private wish, a verbal invitation, or an agreed event?
What would make the characters discuss expectations, clear consent and boundaries before any encounter?
If a one-night encounter never happens, how does the person respond without pressure or resentment?
Which women work with the lead, including younger developers, testers, analysts and managers?
Who is the HR executive and who is the senior HR business partner?
Are the female colleagues friends, mentors, rivals or merely acquaintances of the lead?
Which female colleagues have independent romantic storylines with adult office men?
Who has authority over hiring, ratings, promotions and complaints, and how do those boundaries affect office relationships?
Which society helpers, gym trainers, event coordinators and elders interact with the lead in person?
Which visitors enter through genuinely established events rather than implausible accidental meetings?
Which society men feel physical, romantic, short-term or no attraction toward her?
Who does the lead notice in her society, and what is the reason for any reciprocal interest?
Which other lead's society twins or helpers know her, and through which specific event?
Which of the other four women's husbands interact with this lead, and where do they meet?
How does Soniya's husband join the shared couples' friendship circle?
Which married men experience admiration, physical curiosity, short-term desire or romantic feelings for her?
Does she feel anything toward these men, or only value their friendship and reliability?
What social consequences would follow if a married friend's one-sided attraction became obvious?
Which younger adult devars and sisters live in or visit the lead's household?
Are any adult family members privately attracted to the lead, and is it strictly one-sided?
Which fathers-in-law or older family friends have cross-household admiration or attraction routes?
How do the characters preserve family roles and avoid reading ordinary caregiving as consent?
Are children included only for everyday family and childcare context, separate from all adult attraction routes?
How do we score each direction separately: female-to-male and male-to-female?
Which contacts are professional admiration only, with no sexual or romantic intent?
Which proposed route is one-time, recurring crush, romantic, mutual or unreciprocated?
How many ordinary meetings occur before the first visible emotional change?
Is each attraction's reason, event entry point, approval status and next episode clearly recorded?
